fix(openai, xai): accept Responses stream events larger than 64 MiB (#25510)

## Background

#25463 limits a single server-sent event to 64 MiB in
`parseJsonEventStream`. Its Future Work notes that
`createEventSourceResponseHandler` doesn't expose `maxEventSize` yet, in
case a legitimate stream needs a larger event.

OpenAI Responses is one, and xAI Responses has the same shape.
`response.completed` repeats every output item, and that includes the
base64 `result` of each `image_generation_call`. A turn that generates
several large images (for example 4 high-quality 3840x2160 PNGs with
`gpt-image-2`, about 83 MiB of base64) produces a `response.completed`
event over 64 MiB. All images stream as tool results first. Then the
stream fails with `ParseError: Buffered data exceeded max buffer size of
67108864 characters`, so the caller gets an error part instead of a
finish with usage. A single 1024x1024 image is fine.

## Summary

- `createEventSourceResponseHandler` takes an optional `{ maxEventSize
}` and passes it to `parseJsonEventStream`. Without it, the 64 MiB
default applies as before.
- The OpenAI and xAI Responses language models stream with
`maxEventSize: 512 * 1024 * 1024`, the same bound the gateway video
model uses for its result event (about the maximum length of a string in
V8). Streams keep a bound, so the out-of-memory protection from #25463
still applies, just at a higher limit for this endpoint.
- xAI's `response.completed` also repeats each `image_generation_call`
with its base64 `result` (see `xai-image-generation-tool.1.chunks.txt`),
so it gets the same limit.
- Chat and completion streams are unchanged.
- Azure uses `OpenAIResponsesLanguageModel` for Responses, so it gets
the same limit.

## Why 512 MiB

#25463 bounded events so that a hostile or broken server can't make the
process buffer data until it runs out of memory. This keeps a bound, but
a higher one for Responses only:

- Chat and completion streams, and every other provider, keep the 64 MiB
default. Only the Responses stream, which needs it, goes up.
- 512 * 1024 * 1024 characters is about the maximum length of a string
in V8. A `response.completed` event over that size can't be parsed in
any case, so no smaller limit would keep a valid response working that
this one rejects.
- It's the bound #25463 already chose for the gateway video result
event, which has the same shape: one event that carries every generated
base64 result.
- The tradeoff is that a hostile endpoint behind a custom `baseURL` can
make a Responses stream buffer up to 512 MiB before it fails, instead of
64 MiB. That's still a hard limit, so the uncatchable crash from #25463
can't come back. It can only exhaust a heap smaller than the limit.

## Verification

- `packages/provider-utils`: new `createEventSourceResponseHandler`
tests: an event over `maxEventSize` fails with
`max-buffer-size-exceeded`, an event within it parses, and an event
parses without the option. 59 tests pass on Node.js and on the edge
runtime.
- `packages/openai`: a new `doStream` test streams a
`response.completed` event of about 65 MiB, with an
`image_generation_call` result, in several chunks. It finishes with
usage and no error part. It fails without the change (`ParseError`).
`openai-responses-language-model.test.ts`: 405 tests pass, and the new
test also passes on the edge runtime.
- `packages/xai`: the same `doStream` test for the xAI Responses model,
which also fails without the change.
`xai-responses-language-model.test.ts`: 116 tests pass, and the new test
also passes on the edge runtime.
- `tsc --noEmit` for all three packages and `oxfmt --check` on the
touched files pass.

The 4-image case above was reproduced against the real OpenAI Responses
API through the current release. It hasn't been re-run against this
branch end to end yet. The xAI case is inferred from the shape of the
stream and wasn't reproduced live.

## ai@7.0.182

### Patch Changes

- ac22e59: fix(ai): truncate the realtime audio item that is actually
playing when the user interrupts

On barge-in, WebSocket realtime sessions sent
`conversation-item-truncate` for the most recently received audio item,
with an offset measured from when playback started rather than from the
start of that item. When a short spoken preamble was queued ahead of the
answer (for example before a tool call), interrupting near the end of
the answer was rejected by the provider (`Audio content of 12950ms is
already shorter than 13957ms`), and other interruptions silently cut the
wrong item or at the wrong position. Playback now tracks the item and
in-item position of each scheduled audio chunk, including across
playback underruns, and truncates that item at the position the user
heard.

## ai@7.0.182

### Patch Changes

- ac22e59: fix(ai): truncate the realtime audio item that is actually
playing when the user interrupts

On barge-in, WebSocket realtime sessions sent
`conversation-item-truncate` for the most recently received audio item,
with an offset measured from when playback started rather than from the
start of that item. When a short spoken preamble was queued ahead of the
answer (for example before a tool call), interrupting near the end of
the answer was rejected by the provider (`Audio content of 12950ms is
already shorter than 13957ms`), and other interruptions silently cut the
wrong item or at the wrong position. Playback now tracks the item and
in-item position of each scheduled audio chunk, including across
playback underruns, and truncates that item at the position the user
heard.

feat(provider/openai): add batch output file expiry and expose file ids on status (#25461)

## Background

The OpenAI Batch API lets callers set a TTL on a batch's output and
error files (`output_expires_after` on `POST /batches`), but the
`@ai-sdk/openai` batch adapter had no way to pass it, so those files
always used OpenAI's default retention. Callers also couldn't see which
files a batch produced without calling OpenAI directly.

## Summary

This lets callers bound batch output retention and exposes the output
and error file IDs on batch status and list results.

- New batch provider option `outputFileExpiresAfter` (seconds, integer,
3600 to 2,592,000 inclusive, OpenAI's bounds, same as
`inputFileExpiresAfter`). When set, `POST /batches` includes
`output_expires_after: { anchor: 'created_at', seconds }`, which OpenAI
applies to both the output and the error file, measured from each file's
creation. When unset, the request body is unchanged.
- `doGetBatchStatus` and each `doListBatches` item now return
`providerMetadata.openai.outputFileId` and
`providerMetadata.openai.errorFileId`, each present only when OpenAI
returns a non-empty value. With neither, `providerMetadata` is omitted.
Start results are unchanged.

The option is read from the batch-level `providerOptions.openai` (for
providers created with an Azure name, `providerOptions.azure` first,
then `openai`), like `inputFileExpiresAfter`. The bounds are OpenAI's.
The provider docs' Batch section now lists both expiry options and the
status/list metadata.

## End-to-End Verification

Exercised the real OpenAI Batch API (`/v1/responses` endpoint,
`gpt-5-mini`) through the provider's `experimental_batch()` built from
this checkout. Prerequisite: `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the environment.

```bash
pnpm exec turbo build --filter=@ai-sdk/openai...
cd examples/ai-functions
node --input-type=module < /tmp/openai-batch-output-expiry-complete.mjs           # with outputFileExpiresAfter: 172800
TTL=none node --input-type=module < /tmp/openai-batch-output-expiry-complete.mjs  # without the option
```

Running from `examples/ai-functions` resolves `@ai-sdk/openai` to the
workspace package (`packages/openai/dist/index.js`, printed by a first
probe run of the same flow).

<details><summary>Script</summary>

```js
import { createOpenAI } from '@ai-sdk/openai';

const batch = createOpenAI().experimental_batch();
const auth = { authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY}` };
const ttl = Number(process.env.TTL ?? 172_800);

const started = await batch.doStartBatch({
  requests: [
    {
      id: 'one',
      type: 'text',
      modelId: 'gpt-5-mini',
      options: {
        prompt: [{ role: 'user', content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'Say hi.' }] }],
        maxOutputTokens: 64,
      },
    },
  ],
  ...(process.env.TTL === 'none'
    ? {}
    : { providerOptions: { openai: { outputFileExpiresAfter: ttl } } }),
});
console.log('started', started.batchId, 'createdAt', started.createdAt);

let status;
for (let i = 0; i < 60; i++) {
  status = await batch.doGetBatchStatus({ batchId: started.batchId });
  if (status.status !== 'pending') break;
  await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 20_000));
}
console.log('status:', JSON.stringify(status));

for (const fileId of Object.values(status.providerMetadata?.openai ?? {})) {
  const file = await fetch(`https://api.openai.com/v1/files/${fileId}`, {
    headers: auth,
  }).then(r => r.json());
  console.log(
    'file',
    fileId,
    'expires_at',
    file.expires_at,
    'expires_at - created_at =',
    file.expires_at == null ? null : file.expires_at - file.created_at,
  );
}
```

</details>

Results (the script reads each file ID that `doGetBatchStatus` returned
with `GET /v1/files/{id}`):

| Run | `doGetBatchStatus` `providerMetadata` | output file `expires_at
- created_at` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| without the option | `{ openai: { outputFileId: 'file-FpUG…' } }` |
2,592,000 s (OpenAI's 30-day default) |
| `outputFileExpiresAfter: 172800` | `{ openai: { outputFileId:
'file-PrPC…' } }` | 172,800 s (48 h) |

Before this change the option was ignored (the request body never
carried `output_expires_after`) and status had no file IDs. Both batches
completed without errors, so no error file was produced; the error-file
path is covered by unit tests only.

fix(workflow): keep empty text parts that carry provider metadata (#24918)

## Background

`WorkflowAgent` dropped text parts whose `text` was empty, even when the
part carried `providerMetadata` data

For example, the OpenAI provider returns an empty final text part with
`itemId` and `phase: 'final_answer', but that metadata is lost from
`responseMessages` and the stream `messages`.

## Summary

- keep a text part when it has `providerMetadata`, even if its text is
empty
- matches core behavior

## End-to-End Verification

Reproduced with a mock model that returns a tool call followed by an
empty final text part with `providerMetadata`

- **Before the fix**: the final assistant message was missing the empty
text part with its metadata.
- **After the fix**: generate yields roles `['assistant', 'tool',
'assistant']`, and the final assistant message contains
`{"type":"text","text":"","providerMetadata":{"openai":{"itemId":"msg_x","phase":"final_answer"}}}`.
Stream yields `['user', 'assistant', 'tool', 'assistant']` for metadata
on either `text-start` or `text-end`.

refactor(alibaba): declare model capabilities per model ID (#25497)

## Background

Stacked on #25496 (Moonshot), following the model matrix shape from
#25387. The Alibaba catalog decided language capabilities from a prefix
list and a separate set of model IDs, and video request behavior by
parsing the mode and version out of the model ID, for listed models too.

## Summary

- Each language model ID is now one row with `preservedThinking` and
`jsonSchema`. The 15 IDs that were only in the preserved-thinking set
are `documented: false` rows, so they stay out of the exported catalog
and the model ID type as before.
- Embedding models are rows with their `dimensions`.
- Video models are rows that declare `protocol` and `mode` plus the
documented details, instead of reading them off the ID.
- The prefix list and the version parsing remain only as the fallback
for unlisted IDs (dated snapshots, new models).

```ts
'qwen3.7-max': {
  documented: true,
  preservedThinking: true,
  jsonSchema: true,
},

'wan2.7-r2v': {
  protocol: 'wan27',
  mode: 'r2v',
  audioMode: 'Yes',
  resolutionTiers: ['720P', '1080P'],
  durationRange: '2-10s (with video ref), 2-15s',
},
```

No behavior change, no test changes.

Snapshotted the exported catalog, the provider options, and the
language, embedding and video entries for 78 IDs (every listed ID plus
unlisted variants) before and after: byte-identical JSON.

refactor(google-vertex): declare model capabilities per model ID (#25494)

## Background

Follows the model matrix shape from #25387 (OpenAI), #25435 (Anthropic),

settings and capabilities from the model ID (`startsWith('gemini-')`,
`startsWith('chirp')`, `includes('-live')`, `startsWith('veo-3')`), for
listed models too, and split them across two files.

- Every operation is now one matrix of model IDs by capability, in the
new `google-vertex-model-matrix.ts`. The builders that turn a row into a
catalog entry stay in `google-vertex-model-catalog.ts`.
- A Gemini language row names the Google model it extends. The builder
takes that model's entry from `@ai-sdk/google` and applies the Vertex
restrictions (`serviceTier: false`) on top.
- Image, embedding, video, speech and transcription rows declare what
the ID checks used to decide (`api`, `endpoint`, `mode`,
`generateAudio`, ...). Batch and live transcription share one `mode`
cell.
- Anthropic, xAI and MaaS models are rows as well. Known Anthropic IDs
without declared capabilities are `documented: false` rows instead of
`undefined`.
- The ID checks remain only as the fallback for unlisted IDs (new
models, tuned models, endpoints).

'gemini-2.5-pro': { googleModelId: 'gemini-2.5-pro' },

  api: 'gemini',
  mode: 'live',
  duration: false,

chore(openai): align model catalog capabilities with live API audit (#25462)

## Background

We ran a live audit of the OpenAI model catalog: every declared
capability cell was checked against OpenAI's docs and probed against the
API through the SDK. A handful of cells contradicted what the API
actually does, and a few listed model IDs now come back as
model-not-found. The API result is the source of truth here, so this PR
fixes the catalog values that were wrong. The catalog shape stays the
same.

The audit files are here: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/25485

## Summary

Catalog values corrected to match the live API:

- `flexProcessing` → `false`: `gpt-6.2-astra` and `gpt-6.2-sol`. The API
rejects `service_tier=flex` for these models.
- `chatFunctionToolsWithReasoning` → `false`: all GPT-6 models plus
`gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.4-mini`, and `gpt-5.4-nano`. Chat
Completions returns "Function tools with reasoning_effort are not
supported".
- `configurationUpdates` → `true`: `gpt-5.6`, `gpt-5.6-luna`,
`gpt-5.6-sol`, and `gpt-5.6-terra`. The API accepts request-level
configuration updates.
- `priorityProcessing` → `true`: `gpt-5-nano` and `gpt-5.4-nano`. The
API accepts the priority tier.
- Transcription `streaming` → `true`: `whisper-1`, `gpt-4o-transcribe`,
and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`. Realtime transcription accepts them.

New list `openaiDiscontinuedModelIds` for model IDs that the API now
answers with model-not-found: `gpt-5-chat-latest`,
`gpt-5.1-chat-latest`, `gpt-5.2-chat-latest`, `gpt-5.3-chat-latest`,
`gpt-5-codex`, `gpt-5.1-codex`, `gpt-5.1-codex-mini`, `gpt-image-1`,
`dall-e-2`, and `dall-e-3`. Their entries stay in the catalog so
existing model IDs still type-check.

Tests now use the corrected values. Where a test covers a warn-and-omit
path, it uses a model that still lacks that capability. The generated
OpenAI and Azure capability tables were regenerated with `pnpm
generate:model-capabilities-docs`, which
`verify:model-capabilities-docs` requires. No hand-written docs changed.

Audit results this PR leaves alone:
- `MISSING` rows are docs fields the catalog has no column for.
- `UNVERIFIED` rows didn't produce enough evidence.
- Chat rejects `reasoningEffort: 'max'`, but the chat model already
filters `max` out.
- GPT-6 `promptCacheRetention` and `tts-1`/`tts-1-hd` `instructions`:
the API accepts both, but OpenAI documents them as replaced or ignored,
so they stay unsupported.
- The `responsesLogprobsRequireNonReasoning` rows for GPT-4.x come from
a probe that sent a reasoning effort to non-reasoning models.

fix(harness-pi): harden temporary configuration by using `mkdtemp` (#25457)

## Background

Pi sessions used a deterministic host-side agent directory, which could
cause session setup to depend on configuration outside the caller's
configured agent directory.

## Summary

- Give each Pi session a private, unique temporary root and remove it
when the session is destroyed.
- Avoid implicit model configuration and system-prompt loading from the
harness-owned directory while preserving caller-supplied `agentDir`
behavior.
- Add regression coverage for per-session isolation and disabled
implicit configuration loading.
